R421.note: Gate::authorize throws/403s on denial, closing the ignored-result gap; discloses the OrderPolicy precondition.

R422.note: Correct pg parameterized IN-clause with generated placeholders bound to ids; matches contract.

R423.note: AST allowlist blocks calls/attrs/imports; allows a few extra literal/operator node types beyond arithmetic but nothing unsafe or contract-breaking.

R424.note: Parameterized SqlCommand preserves row count, tenant scope, and string-based date handling as before.

R425.note: Explicitly invokes the model's magic-byte validator before create(), closing the full_clean() bypass without changing behavior for valid files.

R426.note: Bounds check now uses segment.size() instead of the untrusted claimedCapacity; leaves the parameter unused but openly says so, no behavior change.

R427.note: realpath()+prefix-with-separator containment check correctly blocks stream wrappers, absolute paths, and traversal while preserving normal reads.

R428.note: Right library (gorilla/csrf) but no concrete, compilable wiring; describes manually extracting a token and 'passing it to the middleware's validation', which doesn't match how csrf.Protect() actually works.

R429.note: record.at() bounds-checks the write and fails safe via exception instead of corrupting memory; standard CWE-787 remediation shape.

R430.note: Moving storage off the Views tree and randomizing the filename correctly kills Razor auto-execution, but the file's own comment says templates are later 'rendered when a notification email is sent' from Views/EmailTemplates by name -- relocating and renaming breaks that lookup, and the write-up doesn't flag that downstream code must be updated to use the new path/GUID.

R431.note: permission_classes = [IsAdminUser] correctly overrides the AllowAny default for all CRUD actions.

R432.note: Reordering to call login_user() before writing the guest cart id into session matches the case's own designed fixation scenario; no other behavior change.

R433.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() with safe fallback (raw reading) for invalid indices; legitimate indices unaffected.

R434.note: Restores real HS256 verification with a required secret; added try/except for malformed/expired tokens is a disclosed, sensible robustness improvement.

R435.note: Standard PDO prepare/execute parameterization, same return shape.

R436.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset() destroys the aliased Resource; return value unchanged from original intent.

R437.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare enforces exact-length equality, matching the contract precisely (verified: differing lengths return 0).

R438.note: Absolute-path/traversal rejection plus Clean()+prefix-with-separator containment check on an absolute base; correct and standard.

R439.note: Escaping closes the XSS but also removes the ability to render intended rich HTML implied by the 'descriptionHtml' field name and the contract's 'if rich text is supported, allowed formatting survives'; the write-up does openly flag this as a known follow-up requiring a sanitizer library.

R440.note: preg_replace_callback with a strict allowlist and safe default removes the /e code-execution path; deviation from a requested non-allowlisted formatter is disclosed in code and prose.

R441.note: XmlResolver = null is the recognized XmlDocument XXE mitigation; write-up doesn't note .NET Core already defaults XmlResolver to null, but the explicit setting is harmless and correct either way.

R442.note: Moves the state-changing route to the CSRF-protected mux; profile route, 202 response, and method handling all untouched.

R443.note: @EnableMethodSecurity activates the pre-existing @PreAuthorize('hasRole(ADMIN)') annotation on the vulnerable method; correct root-cause fix, no other config changed.

R444.note: Only rejects symlinks whose resolved target escapes uploadsDir; the contract also requires rejecting any requestedName that simply names a symlink (even one resolving inside the dir), which this fix does not check via Lstat. Legitimate direct-file reads are unaffected.

R445.note: expr-eval correctly blocks calls/imports/process access (verified), but expr.evaluate(order) passes the order object itself as the top-level context, so the contract's own example 'order.total + order.tax' throws 'undefined variable: order' instead of returning a number (verified against expr-eval) -- silently breaks the stated legitimate case, undisclosed.

R446.note: check_password() is the right general API, but the file's own docstring says User.password holds plaintext copied by a legacy migration, never Django-hashed -- check_password() will fail to parse that format for every existing user, silently breaking all legitimate logins; no migration/legacy-compare path is provided and the write-up doesn't flag this.

R447.note: @DeleteMapping puts the route behind CsrfFilter, but the file's own comment says the endpoint exists so a plain HTML link (no JS) can trigger deletion; browsers cannot issue DELETE from a link, so the described legitimate use is broken and the write-up never mentions the client needs to change to a JS-driven request.

R448.note: catch block calls next(error) but the route handler is declared as async (req, res) => {...} with no next parameter in scope, so this throws ReferenceError: next is not defined on every error path instead of delegating to the error middleware -- an undisclosed regression, likely worse than the original leak (hung request or crash vs. a verbose response).

R449.note: PreparedStatement with setString replaces string concatenation; return type/usage preserved as noted.

R450.note: Writes to a temp name, verifies actual content via file-type magic bytes, then renames with a server-controlled extension before responding; rejects and cleans up on mismatch. Preserves the success response shape.

R451.note: org.springframework.security.web.csrf.SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler is not a real shipped Spring Security class -- Spring's own docs show this as a custom class you write yourself extending CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler, not an importable framework type. csrf.spa() is also not a real DSL method. As written this would not compile.

R452.note: Synthetic OWASP Benchmark case with no real stored-procedure semantics to preserve; parameterized CallableStatement with setString correctly removes the injection point.

R453.note: Reuses the existing escapeAuthorName() HTML-escaper on rawComment, matching the already-safe authorName handling; comment field has no indicated rich-HTML requirement.

R454.note: Paths.get().normalize()+startsWith() containment check is standard and correct; the thrown IOException on traversal is caught by the file's existing catch(Exception) handler, matching its established error-handling pattern.

R455.note: Replaces the raw socket / hand-built RESP command with StackExchange.Redis's IDatabase.StringSet, which frames arguments safely; same key, same effective SET semantics, same unconditional Ok() response.

R456.note: crypto/rand.Text() (Go 1.24+) is a real, appropriate CSPRNG token API; format string and session-id structure preserved.

R457.note: Adds the missing per-event admin role check, silently rejecting non-admins consistent with the file's existing validation style.

R458.note: Verified by running the sandbox: the regex blocklist (which checks literal substrings like 'process', 'Constructor(') is trivially bypassed via emit.constructor('return this[\'pro\'+\'cess\']')(), which returns the real outer-realm process object (confirmed matching pid) -- vm.runInNewContext already exposed this escape via any passed-in function reference, and the added validation does not close it. Also risks false-positive rejection of benign scripts containing words like 'process' in comments/strings.

R459.note: Tika content-sniffing plus ImageIO re-encode and CREATE_NEW correctly replaces the spoofable Content-Type check; server-controlled name/extension avoids client influence.

R460.note: Standard SqlCommand.Parameters.Add parameterization, same query result and control flow.
